ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider by Ryde voucher and send the driver's account to Ryde for review of abuse of the "I'm Here"/cancellation button + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a driver-cancelled trip on which the driver claimed rider no-show, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is valid only if NS-1's three cumulative conditions are met; NS-0 routes the claim through NS-1 and nothing else [F3][F6][NS-0]. The fee therefore stands or falls with NS-1.

The GPS record settles NS-1(i)–(iii) against the driver. His closest approach to the pickup point in the whole window was 873 m and he never came within 200 m [F1]; at the moment of the "I'm Here" tap (22:37:20) he was 1000 m from the pickup point and spent 0 s inside the radius afterwards [F5], and the only long stationary stretch (22:37:00–22:42:00) was likewise 1000 m away [F2]. NS-1(ii) and (iii) therefore fail on the platform's own record, and the platform never logged an arrival at all (driver_arrived_at null) [F4][NS-1].

The driver's contrary material cannot rescue the fee. His post-trip statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" [F12] and his 22:37 chat "Reached already, blue Toyota Prius, come out please" [F8] are both contradicted by the GPS track [F2][F5]; system records (gps / timeline) control over statements, so neither establishes NS-1(ii) or (iii) [NS-1]. The rider's 22:38 message "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?" [F9] is corroborated by the record that no vehicle came within 200 m [F1].

NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) not being satisfied, NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full [F3][F6][NS-2]. The amount is exactly the cancellation fee recorded on the fare, $6.61; there is no mileage computation because this is a fee dispute, not a route deviation, and no segment_findings arise [F6][NS-2].

NS-2 further attaches an account flag when the driver confirmed arrival while GPS placed him away from the pickup point: he tapped "I'm Here" 1000 m out [F5], which is the meeting-point abuse of the arrival/cancellation button, so flag_account is required [F5][F1][NS-2]. His 90-day profile (2 no-show disputes, both upheld) [F17] only supports that flag and is not used to decide the case; the rider's own profile [F16] is likewise set aside as profile facts never decide a case.

Weather and traffic offer no excuse for stopping a kilometre short: light rain of 1.8 mm [F15] is not a route-related justification, and there were no incidents and no speed-band records in the trip window [F13][F14][RD-4]. On the safety screen, I read every chat message [F8][F9][F10], the complaint and the driver's statement [F12]: the messages are an arrival notice, a query and a cancellation notice — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern is "none" [SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: the chat record is complete with all three messages timestamped [F11] and the GPS trace covers the wait to the cancellation without a hole [F5], so no element of the ruling rests on a missing record [NS-1][NS-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The requested flag_account is granted, but not on the ground the rider pleads for the profile element: RD-6's 90-day 'repeated' counting window is an unpublished rule (G4), and profile facts never decide a case here. The flag rests solely on NS-2's button-abuse limb, settled by F5 (tap 1000 m from pickup) and F1; F17 is support only.

The driver's advocate's own D6 rests the flag partly on the rider's profile F16 (0 upheld disputes), which is irrelevant: F16 cannot establish anything about the driver's conduct, and profile facts cannot alone ground an account action. The refund-plus-flag outcome itself is upheld on F5, F6, F17 under NS-2.
